entities.name: Idomeneus of Lampsacus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Idomeneus of Lampsacus was a prominent Greek philosopher and friend of Epicurus, born in the ancient city of Lampsacus in the Chersonese region of modern-day Turkey around 350 BCE.


He spent many years in Athens, where he studied under the tutelage of Epicurus at his famous garden, and later became a key figure in the development of the Epicurean school of thought.


His teachings emphasized the importance of reason, self-sufficiency, and the pursuit of happiness, and he wrote several works on philosophy, now lost to time.


Despite the lack of concrete evidence about his personal life, Idomeneus of Lampsacus remains an important figure in the history of Western philosophy, and his influence can still be felt in modern debates about ethics, morality, and the human condition.
